question: Anal canal carcinoma arising above the dentate line drains lymphatics to the internal iliac nodes and can spread upward along the rectum, whereas carcinoma below the dentate line drains to the inguinal lymph nodes.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The dentate line divides two lymphatic territories: above → internal iliac nodes; below → inguinal nodes. This is clinically important because inguinal node involvement below the dentate line requires inguinal nodal treatment in addition to pelvic therapy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The dentate line is the embryological junction between hindgut and proctodeum. Above it: internal iliac nodes + superior rectal (endodermal origin). Below it: inguinal nodes (ectodermal origin, somatic lymphatics). This determines the staging and surgical approach for anal cancer.
